notes:
I couldn't write the notes. My first attempt to read the commentary pages failed: the system said I had no web tool uses left for this turn, so I didn't get to read any source.

I had planned to read these pages:
- Enduring Word on Psalm 102 (enduringword.com/bible-commentary/psalm-102/)
- Gill, Ellicott and the Pulpit Commentary on Psalm 102 at biblehub.com
- Precept Austin's Psalm 102 commentary page
- Augustine on this psalm at newadvent.org (his numbering calls it Psalm 101)
- After that, I would have searched for differences between Protestant traditions, netbible.org translation notes, Catholic and Orthodox readings, and the use of vv. 25–27 in Hebrews 1:10–12.

Your rules say to report only what the pages say and to give a URL for every point. Since I read nothing, any verse notes I wrote now would come from my own memory. They wouldn't follow those rules and couldn't be cited, so I haven't written any.

To get this done, you can:
1. **Ask again in a new turn,** and I'll run the research from the start.
2. **Split it up** (for example vv. 1–11, then 12–22, then 23–28, then the tradition and other-view sections). That way each turn needs fewer pages and is less likely to run out.
3. **Paste in text** from any of the pages above, and I'll write the verse-by-verse notes from that, with URLs.
